name: Nintedanib
route_note: Oral capsules twice daily with food

discovery.note: An indolinone angiokinase inhibitor first developed as an anticancer agent.

tagline: Kinase inhibitor that slows progressive fibrosing lung disease
summary: Nintedanib is an oral inhibitor of VEGF, FGF and PDGF receptor tyrosine kinases. It slows lung-function decline in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease and other progressive fibrosing ILDs, and is used with docetaxel in some lung cancers in the EU.
mechanism: Nintedanib binds the ATP pocket of VEGFR1–3, FGFR1–3 and PDGFRα/β, as well as Src-family kinases and others, blocking downstream signalling.

In fibrotic lung disease this reduces fibroblast proliferation, migration and differentiation into myofibroblasts and extracellular matrix deposition. In tumours, the same receptors drive angiogenesis.
uses: Chronic fibrosing interstitial lung diseases with a progressive phenotype
Advanced adenocarcinoma non-small-cell lung cancer with docetaxel (Vargatef, EU)

history.title: INPULSIS trials
history.detail: Two phase 3 trials show nintedanib reduces the annual decline in FVC in IPF.

history.title: US approval
history.detail: FDA approves Ofev for IPF in October; EMA approves Vargatef for NSCLC in November.

history.title: EU approval for IPF
history.detail: Ofev is approved in the European Union.

history.title: Systemic sclerosis ILD
history.detail: FDA approves nintedanib for SSc-ILD based on the SENSCIS trial.

history.title: Progressive fibrosing ILD
history.detail: Approved for chronic fibrosing ILDs with a progressive phenotype after the INBUILD trial.

history.title: Paediatric use
history.detail: FDA approves Ofev for children aged 6 years and older with fibrosing ILD.

pk.metabolism: Esterase hydrolysis to BIBF 1202, then UGT glucuronidation; minor CYP3A4; P-gp substrate

facts: Nintedanib is sold under two brands: Ofev for lung fibrosis and Vargatef for lung cancer.
It was approved for IPF on the same day as pirfenidone.
